title: Design a Text Editor
spaceBreakdown:
- string left: up to n characters (n = total text across all calls) → O(n)
- string right: up to n characters → O(n)
- recursion depth: none
- not counted: returned substrings (≤ 10 chars each)
approach: Maintain two strings: `left` (text before cursor, in order) and `right` (text after cursor, stored reversed). All mutations happen at the back of either string - `push_back`/`pop_back` are O(1) amortized. Moving the cursor left shifts characters from the back of `left` to the back of `right`; moving right does the reverse. The last-10-chars query is a simple `substr` from the back of `left`. Every operation is O(k) where k ≤ 40.
hints: When the cursor sits in the middle of the text, which characters actually change during each operation - only those adjacent to the cursor, or the entire text?

Use two strings: `left` for text before the cursor and `right` for text after it (stored in reverse). Moving the cursor left shifts characters from the back of `left` to the back of `right` - e.g., with `left="leetpractice"`, `cursorLeft(8)` pops 8 chars off `left` and pushes them onto `right`, leaving `left="leet"`.

```
addText(text):     append text to left
deleteText(k):     actual = min(k, |left|); resize left; return actual
cursorLeft(k):     move min(k,|left|) chars from back of left to back of right
                   return last min(10,|left|) chars of left
cursorRight(k):    move min(k,|right|) chars from back of right to back of left
                   return last min(10,|left|) chars of left
```

**Delete beyond available** - left has fewer characters than k
`["TextEditor","addText","deleteText"], [[],["ab"],[5]]` → `Expected: [null,null,2]`
⚠️ Bug: returning k instead of min(k, left.size()) → returns 5

**Cursor left at position 0** - cursor already at leftmost, left becomes empty
`["TextEditor","addText","cursorLeft"], [[],["abc"],[10]]` → `Expected: [null,null,""]`
⚠️ Bug: not clamping move count to left.size(), popping from empty string → undefined behavior

**Return fewer than 10 chars** - left has only 1 char after the move
`["TextEditor","addText","cursorLeft"], [[],["ab"],[1]]` → `Expected: [null,null,"a"]`
⚠️ Bug: always calling substr(size-10) without min(10,size) → substr with wrapped index, crash

**Cursor right at end** - right string is empty, cursor cannot move
`["TextEditor","addText","cursorRight"], [[],["abc"],[10]]` → `Expected: [null,null,"abc"]`
⚠️ Bug: not clamping move count to right.size(), popping from empty right → undefined behavior

followUps.q: If k and text.length can be up to 10^5 with 10^5 calls, how would you optimize beyond O(k) per call?
followUps.a: Replace the two strings with a balanced BST (rope) where each node stores a substring and its subtree size. Split and merge run in O(log n), so cursor moves become O(log n) instead of O(k). The last-10-chars query walks from the cursor split point using subtree sizes. Total time drops to O(Q log n).

followUps.q: What if you need to support selecting a range of text and copying it?
followUps.a: Track a selection start position alongside the cursor. Copying extracts the characters between the two positions from `left` and/or `right`, costing O(selection length). With a rope, you can split out the selected range in O(log n) and read it without copying.

followUps.q: What if the editor must support undo/redo for all operations?
followUps.a: Push each operation onto an undo stack with enough info to reverse it: addText stores the text length (undo = deleteText), deleteText stores the deleted text (undo = addText at cursor), cursor moves store k (undo = opposite direction). Redo uses a parallel stack. Space is O(total text ever inserted) in the worst case.
